newsitem.title: FRANCE: Best French wheat bid covers 10,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Best French wheat bid covers 10,000 tonnes.

text.p: The best bid for European Union soft wheat through France on Thursday covered a tiny volume of 10,000 tonnes but bids spanning the first four Ecus in subsidy were for a combined total of 182,200 tonnes, grain traders said.
Exporters bid for 10,000 tonnes of wheat with at an EU refund of 4.74 Ecus per tonne, they said.
In higher tranches, bids up to and including 5.74 Ecus per tonne were for 37,500 tonnes. Bids up to 6.74 Ecus were for 67,500 tonnes. Those up to 7.75 Ecus were for 182,500 tonnes.
Higher up the subsidy scale, bids up to and including 9.45 Ecus were for 185,500 tonnes.
French grains office ONIC said earlier the full range of bids was for 290,500 tonnes of EU soft wheat at refunds between 4.74 Ecus and 14.99 Ecus per tonne.
Traders said the lowest subsidy bid in France implied a high $170 per tonne on world markets for May.
But with few bids packed at the lowest end of the range -- unlike in previous weeks -- Thursday's EU wheat auction would effectively start around 7.75 Ecus, worth $167 per tonne abroad.
Barring unseen heavy bidding elsewhere, French bids suggested Thursday's wheat subsidies might be capped around 8.75 Ecus, giving a world price of $166 fob France, traders said.
That would be above the last award pegged at $160 per tonne and well above benchmark soft red winter of around $154 a tonne.
French domestic prices are a touch firmer than at the last tender two weeks ago, with May around 902.50 francs delivered Rouen (plus first-half May carrying charges of 69.08 francs).
The one-month forward dollar has eased from around 5.67 French francs at the previous tender to 5.62 francs today.
